environment.tool: manual audit of the final tag source + live compiled binary; raw-socket client sending exact bytes, strict-token upstream peer logging verbatim request bytes and byte count

findings.description: After the identity-AE attack, a victim with Accept-Encoding: gzip is served the poisoned entry at zero new fetches (captured upstream count stays at 4; the hit body is the identity LINE with EXEC:0 because this run's overwrite came from a clean earlier fetch of the same raw target). Re-attack without any Accept-Encoding header stores under base|* (enc() is empty), and the following no-AE victim is then served at zero fetches, confirming the store-side wildcard arm is reachable from a no-AE attacker too. 6baf167b refetches on both cross-AE victims, which is exactly its intended negative contrast.
findings.title: Wildcard arm confirmed at zero fetch: gzip and no-AE victims are served the identity-AE poison; no-AE attack stores under |*

limitations: All RCE in this corpus is RCE on the upstream host
methods: Control request first on the same config
Raw client bytes and raw upstream bytes captured in hex
Payload diffed against the control line
